nwt-john-1-1-a-god: John's Gospel opens: 'In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.' The New World Translation renders the last phrase 'the Word was a god' — which turns a statement that Jesus is God into a statement that he is a lesser divine being. The argument is about Greek grammar and a missing definite article, and this case walks through it in plain terms.
nwt-colossians-other-inserted: Colossians 1:16–17 says that by Jesus all things were created and that he is before all things. If that stands, he cannot himself be a created thing. The New World Translation inserts the word 'other' four times — 'all other things' — which makes him one created being among many. In the 1950 edition the additions were bracketed as insertions; in later editions the brackets came off.
nwt-jehovah-inserted-nt: Jehovah's Witnesses are right about something important: God's personal name, YHWH, appears thousands of times in the Hebrew Bible and most English translations replace it with 'the LORD.' Restoring it is defensible. The difficulty is the New Testament, where the New World Translation prints 'Jehovah' 237 times — even though no Greek manuscript of the New Testament contains the name anywhere.
nwt-john-8-58-i-have-been: In John 8:58 Jesus says 'Before Abraham was, I am' — and his hearers immediately pick up stones, because 'I AM' is the name God gives himself in Exodus 3. The New World Translation renders it 'I have been,' which turns a divine self-identification into a statement about age. This case examines the Greek and why the crowd reacted as it did.
nwt-hebrews-1-8-throne: Hebrews 1 argues that the Son is greater than the angels, and verse 8 quotes the Father addressing him: 'Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever.' The New World Translation reverses subject and predicate — 'God is your throne' — which removes the address. This case examines the Greek construction and how every other major translation reads it.
nwt-luke-23-43-comma: Jesus tells the dying thief, 'Verily I say unto thee, To day shalt thou be with me in paradise.' Witnesses do not believe anyone goes to heaven at death, so the New World Translation moves the comma: 'Truly I tell you today, you will be with me in Paradise.' Ancient Greek had no punctuation, so this is a real interpretive question — and this case examines how Luke uses the phrase elsewhere.
nwt-john-14-14-me-deleted: In John 14:14 Jesus says, in the best manuscripts, 'If ye shall ask any thing in my name, me I will do it' — praying to Jesus. Since Witnesses hold that prayer belongs to Jehovah alone, the New World Translation drops the word 'me,' even though the manuscript support for it is strong. This case examines the textual evidence.
nwt-committee-anonymity-credentials: The New World Translation was produced by a committee whose members were never named — the organization says this was for humility. Names later emerged, and only one had studied biblical languages formally: Fred Franz, who had two years of classical Greek and no Hebrew training. Under oath in a Scottish court in 1954 he was asked to translate a verse into Hebrew and declined.
chron-607-vs-587: This is the foundation stone of the entire religion, so it is worth understanding. The Watchtower dates Jerusalem's destruction by Babylon to 607 BC, adds 2,520 years, and arrives at 1914 — the year Christ supposedly began ruling invisibly. Every other source — thousands of dated Babylonian business tablets, astronomical records, king lists — puts the destruction at 587/586 BC.
chron-2011-articles-vat4956: In 2011 the Watchtower published a defense of 607 built on a Babylonian astronomical tablet called VAT 4956, which records lunar and planetary positions for a specific year of Nebuchadnezzar's reign. The articles accepted some observations on the tablet and set others aside. This case examines the tablet and what happens when you use all of its data rather than part of it.
chron-jonsson-gentile-times: In the 1970s a Swedish elder named Carl Olof Jonsson was asked a question about 607 he could not answer, so he spent years researching it and submitted his findings to headquarters. He was disfellowshipped. His work was published as The Gentile Times Reconsidered. This case examines both the research and the response to it — no published rebuttal has ever engaged it directly.
dates-1874-1914-retrofit: Almost no Witness has been told this. Until 1943 the organization taught that Christ's invisible presence began in 1874, not 1914 — and 1914 was published as the year the world would end. An 1889 book said the battle of the great day of God would end in 1914 with the complete overthrow of earth's rulership. When it didn't, the date was kept and its meaning replaced.
dates-1925-beth-sarim: In the early 1920s the organization taught that 1925 would bring the resurrection of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, under the slogan 'Millions Now Living Will Never Die.' In 1929 it bought a San Diego mansion, Beth Sarim, and deeded it to those patriarchs for their return. Its president Joseph Rutherford lived in it. The house was sold in 1948, and the organization's own history book discusses it.
dates-1975: Watchtower publications in the late 1960s calculated that six thousand years of human history would end in 1975 and pointed to what that might mean. Members sold homes, quit jobs and postponed education. Nothing happened. In 1980 the organization acknowledged that its own publications had built the expectation — an unusually direct admission that this case works from.
dates-generation-1914-redefined: Jesus said 'this generation shall not pass, till all these things be fulfilled.' The Watchtower applied it to people alive in 1914, and for decades the Awake! masthead promised a world without end before that generation passed away. As those people died the definition was revised — in 1995, in 2008, and in 2010 into two 'overlapping' generations. This case tracks the revisions.
dates-early-cluster-1878-1881-1918: 1914, 1925 and 1975 are the famous ones. Before them came others: 1878, when the saints were to be caught up to heaven; 1881, when the same expectation was moved; and 1918, predicted in the book The Finished Mystery. None happened. This case collects the forgotten dates, because the pattern matters more than any single failure.
auth-fds-2012-governing-body: In Matthew 24:45 Jesus describes a faithful and discreet slave appointed over his master's household. The Watchtower reads this as prophecy: Christ inspected all religions in 1919 and appointed the Watch Tower Society. In 2012 the Governing Body announced that the slave is specifically them — the eight or so men at headquarters. This case examines the interpretation and its 2012 narrowing.
auth-light-gets-brighter: Proverbs 4:18 says the path of the righteous is like the light of dawn, growing brighter. The organization uses this to explain doctrinal reversals: the light gets brighter, so understanding is refined. This case examines whether that works as a defense — because if any change can be explained the same way, no teaching can ever be tested by whether it turned out to be true.
auth-organ-transplants-reversal: In 1967 the Watchtower declared organ transplants to be cannibalism and forbade them. In 1980 the ban was lifted and transplants became a matter of conscience. In between, members declined transplants they might have survived with. This case examines the reversal, and the absence of any acknowledgment of harm — which is what makes it a case about authority rather than medicine.
auth-prophet-paradox: This is the sharpest question in the whole section, and it does not require any history. The Governing Body says it is God's sole channel of communication today. It also says it is neither inspired nor infallible. Both statements are published. This case examines what follows: if the channel can be wrong, why is disagreeing with it grounds for losing your family?
avoid-jws-deny-jesus: Many Christians believe Jehovah's Witnesses do not believe in Jesus. They do — they believe he is God's first creation, that he died for sins, and that he now rules God's kingdom. The disagreement is about who he is, not whether he matters. This case exists because opening with a false claim tells a Witness immediately that you do not know what they believe.
avoid-russell-freemason: Claims that Charles Taze Russell was a Freemason, or that the winged-sun symbol on his grave proves occult ties, circulate widely. The evidence does not support it: he used the word 'mason' in a spiritual sense in a sermon, and the pyramid monument was erected by the Society after his death. This case explains why this is a distraction from far stronger documented material.
avoid-1994-prediction: The claim that the Watchtower predicted the world would end in 1994 gets repeated often. It did not — that prediction belongs to Harold Camping and Family Radio, an entirely separate organization. The Watchtower's real failed dates are numerous and documented. This case exists because attributing the wrong one hands a Witness an easy correction.
jesus-michael-archangel: Witnesses teach that Jesus is Michael the archangel — a created spirit being, the first of God's creations, who became a man and then returned to that state. This is the doctrine most other differences flow from, because it decides whether Jesus is a creature or the Creator. This case examines the texts used for the identification and the ones that stand against it.
bodily-resurrection-denied: Witnesses teach that Jesus was raised as a spirit creature and that his physical body was disposed of. Christian teaching holds he rose bodily — which is why Luke 24 has him showing his hands and feet, inviting touch, and eating fish, and why Thomas is told to put his finger in the wounds. This case examines those passages and the Witness reading of them.
holy-spirit-active-force: Witnesses teach the Holy Spirit is not a person but God's impersonal active force — something like electricity. The New World Translation prints 'holy spirit' in lower case. This case examines the passages where the Spirit does things persons do: speaking, forbidding, being grieved, being lied to, and being named alongside the Father and Son in the baptismal formula.
soul-sleep-annihilationism: Witnesses teach that the dead are unconscious — the soul does not survive the body — and that the wicked are annihilated rather than punished forever. This case takes the position seriously, because it has real biblical support in Ecclesiastes and elsewhere and thoughtful Christians have held versions of it, then examines the texts on the other side.
worship-of-jesus-flipflop: This is one of the most striking reversals in the organization's history. From 1898 into the 1950s Watchtower publications taught that Jesus should be worshipped, and the phrase was written into the Society's own charter. Between 1954 and 1964 the teaching was reversed and worship of Jesus was declared unscriptural. This case works from the publications on both sides.
two-class-salvation-system: Witnesses divide believers into two groups: 144,000 who go to heaven, are born again, and are in the new covenant, and everyone else — the 'great crowd' — who hope to live forever on a paradise earth as God's friends rather than his children. This case examines whether the New Testament knows any such division, since it speaks of one flock, one hope, and one body.
memorial-passing-emblems: Once a year Witnesses observe the Memorial. Bread and wine are passed down the rows — and almost everyone present declines them, because only the 144,000 may partake. At the 2023 Memorial, 21.1 million attended and 23,212 partook. This case examines the practice against Jesus's words at the Last Supper: 'drink ye all of it.'
mediator-only-144000: 1 Timothy 2:5 says there is one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus. Watchtower teaching holds that Christ is mediator specifically for the 144,000, with the great crowd relating to God through the arrangement rather than as parties to the new covenant. This case examines that teaching against the verse, and asks the personal question it raises.
1935-cutoff-abandoned: In 1935 the organization announced that the 144,000 was essentially full, so anyone converting afterwards belonged to the earthly class. That was taught for 72 years. Then the number of people claiming to be anointed began rising, and in 2007 the cutoff was quietly dropped. This case examines a doctrine taught for three generations and then abandoned.
blood-ban-1945-innovation: Witnesses refuse blood transfusions, and it is the belief they are most known for. What surprises most people — including many Witnesses — is that the movement did not hold it for its first 65 years. The prohibition was introduced in 1945. This case examines the texts it rests on, chiefly Acts 15, and the question of whether they address transfusion at all.
blood-fractions-incoherence: The blood policy has been redrawn repeatedly. Whole blood and its four main components are forbidden, but since 2000 fractions taken from those same components — including hemoglobin, which comes from red cells — are a matter of personal conscience. This case examines the line as it currently stands, and the difficulty of explaining it to a doctor or a dying member.
organ-transplants-cannibalism: For thirteen years, from 1967 to 1980, the organization taught that accepting an organ transplant was cannibalism and grounds for discipline. Members refused kidneys and corneas during those years. The policy was then reversed to a matter of conscience with no acknowledgment of the cost. This case documents both the ban and the reversal from Watchtower publications.
vaccination-ban-1931: From 1931 to 1952 the organization opposed vaccination, describing it in its publications as a direct violation of God's everlasting covenant. Members refused vaccines, including for their children, and some faced legal consequences. The position was quietly reversed in 1952. This case sets the ban beside the later blood and transplant policies as part of one pattern.
awake-1994-youths-died: The 22 May 1994 issue of Awake! carried a cover feature titled 'Youths Who Put God First,' celebrating 26 young Jehovah's Witnesses who died rather than accept blood transfusions. Their photographs were printed. This case examines the document itself, because it shows more directly than any argument what the doctrine costs and how the organization presented that cost.
shunning-mechanics-family: A Witness who is expelled — or who simply resigns — is shunned by the entire congregation, including family members who do not live in the same household. Parents cut off adult children; children cut off parents. In 2024 the terminology softened from 'disfellowshipped' to 'removed' and a greeting was permitted. This case examines what changed and what did not.
apostates-mentally-diseased: A 2011 Watchtower described apostates — meaning anyone who persistently disagrees with the Governing Body — as 'mentally diseased,' and instructed members to avoid their words entirely, including online. This case examines the article and what it accomplishes: it makes information itself the danger, which is the mechanism that keeps every other question on this site from being examined.
faders-pimo-exit-costs: There is no neutral way to leave. Formally resigning has been treated exactly like expulsion since 1981, so members who stop believing often 'fade' — quietly reducing attendance — or stay attending while no longer believing, a state ex-members call PIMO, Physically In, Mentally Out. This case examines what that costs a person, and why it exists.
un-ngo-association: The organization identifies the United Nations with the scarlet beast of Revelation and teaches that God's people must stay separate from it. From 1992 to 2001 the Watch Tower Society was registered as an NGO associated with the UN Department of Public Information, which required supporting UN principles. It withdrew days after The Guardian reported it. This case works from the UN's own records.
arc-case-study-29: In 2015 the Australian Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse examined the Jehovah's Witnesses. Using the organization's own case files, it found 1,006 alleged perpetrators recorded since 1950, and that not one had been reported by the organization to police. This case works from the Commission's published findings and the organization's testimony.
abuse-civil-cases: Beyond the Australian inquiry there is a substantial civil litigation record in the United States — including the Conti case in California and cases in Montana and elsewhere — turning on the 'two witnesses' rule, under which an accusation requires two witnesses to be acted on. This case examines the judgments and the policies they examined.
failed-date-prophecies: This case gathers the record in one place: 1878, 1881, 1914, 1918, 1925, 1975, and the repeatedly redefined 1914 generation. Every one was published by the organization, and every one failed. Deuteronomy 18:22 gives one test for a voice claiming to speak for God. This case applies it to the whole sequence rather than to any single date.
birthdays-holidays-ban: Witnesses do not celebrate birthdays, Christmas, Easter or national holidays. The birthday argument rests on the fact that the only two birthday celebrations in the Bible both involve a beheading. This case examines that reasoning, and the broader question of binding every conscience organization-wide where Scripture — Romans 14 in particular — leaves liberty.
higher-education-discouraged: Watchtower publications have long discouraged university education, urging young Witnesses toward pioneering instead. This case examines the counsel as published and its measurable effects: Pew survey data showing Jehovah's Witnesses with the lowest college-graduation rate of any US religious group, and what that means for someone who later leaves without qualifications.
avoid-no-medical-treatment: Jehovah's Witnesses refuse blood transfusions specifically. They accept surgery, chemotherapy, vaccines, transplants and every other form of medical treatment, and many hospitals now maintain bloodless-surgery programmes largely because of them. This case exists because saying they refuse all medicine is false, and a Witness will correct you instantly.
avoid-jws-worship-russell: Witnesses do not worship Charles Taze Russell, and most modern Witnesses know relatively little about him — the organization has distanced itself from much of his teaching. This case exists because the claim is false and because the real point is stronger: what Russell actually taught, and how much of it was quietly abandoned.
avoid-2024-shunning-ended: In 2024 the organization changed its terminology from 'disfellowshipped' to 'removed from the congregation' and permitted members to greet a removed person. Headlines described this as the end of shunning. It was not — normal association, family contact and spiritual fellowship remain cut off. This case explains what changed precisely, so you neither overstate nor dismiss it.
avoid-dismiss-persecution-record: Under the Third Reich, Jehovah's Witnesses were the only group persecuted purely for a religious position they could have ended at any moment by signing a renunciation. Around 10,000 were imprisoned and roughly 1,500 died. In the United States they took more than fifty cases to the Supreme Court and won much of the religious-liberty law every church now relies on. This case is about saying that first.
